pairing_hash_note: Recomputed and checked by tests/contracts/maps/test_map_contracts.py; written by `python3 maps/r4/rehash.py`.

pivot_variables.name: status
notes: Guarded to 'finished'. The Encounter record and its status stay in the source layer (concept note section 6).

pivot_variables.name: classCode
notes: v3-ActCode AMB. Bound so it cannot be dropped silently, but NOT emitted: it has no reviewed entry in the code-interpretation table, and concept note section 2 forbids treating a code literal as a class assertion. ex:ClinicalEncounter comes from the reviewed vocabulary, not from this code.

pivot_variables.name: participantType
notes: Guarded to v3-ParticipationType PPRF. It does NOT type the practitioner role: there is no reviewed participation-type-to-role-class table, which is a new reviewer question.

pivot_variables.name: participantRef
notes: enc-contained-practitioner resolves '#pr-inline' in the containing resource's scope, so its practitioner entity IRI differs from enc-baseline's Practitioner/c7. That is intended: a contained resource has no existence outside its container.

pivot_variables.name: end
notes: Required. An open-ended period fails the source shape rather than materialising a fabricated endpoint; concept note section 2 requires unknown endpoints to be preserved and the pilot has no reviewed representation for one (R3 / Q-A2-3).

repetition_scopes.name: encounter
repetition_scopes.note: One iteration per map run. Encounter.participant is cardinality 1 in v1, not `*`, so there is no repeating triple constraint anywhere except the tolerated, unmapped DomainResource.contained.

node_key_rules._roles_are_keyed_by_the_encounter: Not by the person. Two encounters give two distinct patient-role nodes, because a role is a feature of its holder in the context of one process; merging them would assert one role participating in two processes.
node_key_rules._why: CD-1: no id() in the pinned engine.

terminology_dependencies: NO code-interpretation entry is used. v3-ActCode and v3-ParticipationType have no reviewed entries, so neither code types anything.
status_eligibility_note: Concept note section 6: an in-progress Encounter 'may receive a separate, explicitly defined policy; it is not treated as a finished interval'. That policy is R3 / Q-A2-2 and is unanswered, so in-progress fails the source shape and stays source-only. R3's 2026-10-01 answer widened the Observation maps to amended/corrected; it says nothing about Encounter, which has no revision axis in its status value set. `finished` remains the only eligible Encounter status, and a finished Encounter with an open-ended period still awaits a ruling.
expected_failures: Encounter.period without Period.end (covers enc-open-period, declared source-only)
more than one Encounter.participant -- see limitations below
a participation type other than PPRF
an Encounter.class system other than v3-ActCode
any Encounter element outside the CLOSED shape, including modifierExtension
an ambiguous or unresolvable subject or participant.individual -- no entity is claimed, so no target graph
limitations: EXACTLY ONE PARTICIPANT. Encounter.participant is cardinality 1, not `*`. A second participant fails validation loudly rather than being dropped or cross-joined. This is a ShExMap expressiveness limit, not a modelling choice: each role node needs its own target IRI, that IRI is an identity-service run binding, and ThreadedMaterializer staticVars are global to a materialization -- there is no way to supply one per iteration. DR-302's decomposition does not rescue it, because a FHIR participant is a blank node with no source IRI to root a pass at. Reported to the integration lead; see DR-201.
static_analysis_note: CD-1: no static checker ships and Agent 4's linter has not landed.
Asserted at run time on all four Encounter fixtures by tests/contracts/maps/test_encounter_gate3.py.
entailment: SULO 0.2.12 asserts sulo:hasParticipant owl:propertyChainAxiom (sulo:hasParticipant [owl:inverseOf sulo:hasFeature]), which is hasParticipant o isFeatureOf -> hasParticipant (DR-002, verified against the axiom).

So `encounter hasParticipant person` and `encounter hasParticipant practitioner` are ENTAILED, not asserted. test_encounter_gate3.py computes the entailment from the emitted triples and asserts the map did not assert either of them directly, and that no hasPatient-style shortcut exists.
